text:
kai: quick sync — ran a chaos-sweep across AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 variants focused on structured-output prompts. found a reproducible class of failures where tool-args JSON ends up invalid (unclosed brace / trailing comma) when the model emits escaped backslashes or windows-path-looking strings. :eyes:

maria: can you drop a minimal failing example?

kai: here's one that triggered locally (AWQ q8, deterministic sampling off):
```json
{
  "tool": "open_file",
  "args": "C:\\Users\\alex\\notes.txt",
}
```

devon: dang, trailing comma. is the model literally emitting the comma or is it a chunking/streaming reassembly bug?

kai: short repro notes: the comma appears in the final token sequence. but when we re-run with streaming disabled the output is valid. hypothesis: kv-cache chunk boundary + token-splitting on escaped sequences leads to a partial escape emitted then later a comma appended by the sampler. repro rate ~0.6% across our 10k structured prompt suite for AWQ-q8; GPTQ-int8 shows ~0.12%, FP8 negligible so far.

aisha: steps to reproduce? I can run locally on dedicated pool.

kai: command I used: `./eval_harness --model mistral-7b-awq-q8 --prompts=structured_paths.jsonl --seed=1234 --streaming=on --out=out_awq.jsonl --mutations=escape,comma`

sam: any metrics on correctness impact (funcall exact-match etc)?

kai: short summary from the sweep: exact-match drop on funcall contract for affected prompts: AWQ-q8: -3.1% (10k), GPTQ-int8: -0.8%. invalid_json_rate AWQ-q8: 0.006, GPTQ-int8: 0.0012. these are noisy but consistent across runs.

eval-bot: summary attached -> csv://s3/evals/chaos-sweep/1765234001-summary.csv (sha256: abc123...). key columns: prompt_id, model, config, invalid_json, em_delta.

maria: is this only when outputs include backslashes? what about quotes, unicode escapes?

kai: mostly backslashes and sequences like `\\n`, `\\\"` (escaped quote inside an escaped string). streaming chunking seems to cut in the middle of a multi-char escape sequence, tokenization + AWQ decoding path then misorders or emits an extra comma token in the completion.

devon: could be AWQ decode LUT for byte sequences. any stack traces or runtime logs?

kai: pasted a small debug trace (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T21:02:14Z] kvchunker: flush chunk id=1792 size=768
[2026-03-18T21:02:14Z] decoder-awq: emit tokens (partial escape) => tokens: ["\\", "n", "\"", ","]
[2026-03-18T21:02:14Z] streamer: sent chunk (eof=false)
[2026-03-18T21:02:14Z] sampler: append_token -> "," (token id 42)
[2026-03-18T21:02:14Z] streamer: final chunk (eof=true)
```

aisha: ok that log makes sense w.r.t chunk boundary. can we force the chunker to align on escape boundaries as a short-term mitigation?

kai: yes, one mitigation path: post-process stream reassembly to validate JSON incrementally and hold partial objects until a stable close. another path: change chunk size heuristic to avoid splitting backslash sequences (cheaper).

sam: priority for rollout? customers impacted? :thinking_face:

kai: immediate user-visible failures are in private deployments with streaming enabled and AWQ-q8 runtime. hosted customers using our API see far fewer hits because default models are FP8 or fallback to different routing. still high risk for teams using private with AWQ and function-calling.

devon: I'll take a bisect on the runtime decoding path. starting from commit range `runtime@v2.13.0..v2.14.3` to see where chunker/decoder interplay changed.

aisha: I'll put together a small CI fuzz check: generate strings with backslashes/quotes and validate reassembled JSON across streaming/streaming-off paths. we should fail builds that regress invalid_json_rate by >0.1%.

kai: thanks — plan: 1) devon bisect; 2) aisha add JSON-fuzzer job + short-run chaos test; 3) sam prepare canary config to disable streaming chunking for AWQ q8 in Dedicated, 4) temporary mitigation: server-side reassembly JSON sanitizer. I'll open a tracking ticket.

ci-bot: created INF-2345: "awq-streaming-json-escape-regression" assigned to devon, severity P2

eval-bot: note — add test vectors: paths_with_backslashes.jsonl, nested-escape-cases.jsonl, windows-urls.jsonl. attaching small corpus link -> s3://evals/chaos/escape-corpus.tar.gz

maria: thanks all. ping me when bisect yields a suspect commit. I'll coordinate release notes for Dedicated customers. :+1:

kai: will do. short-term I pushed a dev edge that reassembles stream chunks and runs json.parse on the reassembled payload before returning to clients; we should see invalid_json_rate drop to ~0.0 in smoke runs. please don't roll that edge to prod without review.

devon: bisect started — will post findings in this thread.

sam: adding to oncall queue for 24h observation once canary is live.

[end of thread]
